title: Creating Differential Transcript Expression Results with DESeq2
author: David A Eccles

steps.title: Initialize date and load libraries
steps.instruction: Create analysisDate variable for file naming: `countDate <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%b-%d")`. Load required R packages: `library(tidyverse)`, `library(DESeq2)`, `library(ashr)`, set Java memory with `options(java.parameters = "-Xmx10G")`, and load `library(xlsx)` for Excel output.

steps.title: Identify count files
steps.instruction: List all CSV files matching the pattern "_wide_transcript_counts.*\\.csv$" with `data.files <- list.files(pattern = "_wide_transcript_counts.*\\.csv$")`; assign sample names by stripping the suffix: `names(data.files) <- sub("_wide_transcript_counts.*\\.csv$","",data.files)`. Print `data.files` to verify correct file names.

steps.title: Create empty skeleton tables
steps.instruction: Initialize an empty gene lookup table and an empty raw counts tibble: `geneLookup.tbl <- NULL; counts.raw.tbl <- tibble(tdir=character());`

steps.title: Populate tables from each count file
steps.instruction: For each file in `data.files`, read the CSV, create a combined transcript‑direction identifier, and merge data into the skeleton tables:

substeps.instruction: Read file and add `tdir` column: `data.files[dfi] %>% read_csv %>% mutate(tdir = paste0(transcript, "_", dir)) -> counts.sub.tbl`.
Append gene‑metadata columns (excluding barcode columns) to `geneLookup.tbl`: `geneLookup.tbl %>% rbind(geneLookup.tbl, select(counts.sub.tbl, -contains("BC"), -contains("RB"))) -> geneLookup.tbl`.
Select barcode columns (`BC` and `RB`) plus `tdir` into `counts.sub.tbl`: `counts.sub.tbl %>% select("tdir", contains("BC"), contains("RB")) -> counts.sub.tbl`.
Prefix barcode column names with the sample label: `bcCols % paste0(names(data.files)[dfi], ".", .)` (where `bcCols` is the vector of barcode column names).
Merge the sample’s barcode columns into the master count table: `counts.raw.tbl %>% full_join(counts.sub.tbl, by="tdir") -> counts.raw.tbl`.

steps.title: Remove duplicate gene rows and verify columns
steps.instruction: Deduplicate the gene lookup table: `geneLookup.tbl %>% unique -> geneLookup.tbl`. Check that the column names of `counts.raw.tbl` match expectations with `colnames(counts.raw.tbl)`. Example output includes columns such as `"tdir"`, `"CGAug18_004.BC04"`, etc.

steps.title: Read and clean sample metadata
steps.instruction: Load metadata, convert IDs to character, keep only samples present in the count table, and replace underscores with periods in both metadata IDs and count‑table column names:

substeps.instruction: Filter to samples in the count table: `meta.df %>% filter(SampleID %in% colnames(counts.raw.tbl)) %>% arrange(Condition) -> meta.df`.
Replace '_' with '.' in IDs: `meta.df$SampleID <- gsub("_", ".", meta.df$SampleID)`.
Replace '_' with '.' in count‑table column names: `colnames(counts.raw.tbl) <- gsub("_", ".", colnames(counts.raw.tbl))`.

steps.title: Subset and re‑order count rows
steps.instruction: Select forward‑oriented transcripts, coerce barcode columns to integers, replace NA with 0, ensure distinct rows, join gene annotation, and reorder columns to match metadata sample order:

substeps.instruction: `select(transcript, Chr, Strand, Start, End, Description, Gene, dir, tdir, match(meta.df$SampleID[meta.df$SampleID %in% colnames(.)], colnames(.))) -> filt.count.tbl`.

steps.title: Sort by expression and write raw counts
steps.instruction: Order `filt.count.tbl` by descending row‑sum across all barcode columns (`bcCols`) and write to a CSV named with the analysis date:

steps.title: Reload count and metadata for downstream filtering
steps.instruction: Read the previously written raw counts and metadata again, converting underscores to periods and keeping only matching samples:

substeps.instruction: `countDate % read_csv() -> count.tbl` (note: this line follows the original script).
`meta.df <- read.csv("metadata.csv") %>% mutate(SampleID = gsub("_", ".", as.character(SampleID))) %>% filter(SampleID %in% colnames(count.tbl))`.

steps.title: Filter metadata for 4T1 strain
steps.instruction: Retain only rows where `Strain == "4T1"`, then sort by `Line` and `Replicate`: `meta.df %>% filter(Strain == "4T1") %>% arrange(Line, Replicate) -> meta.df`.

steps.title: Convert metadata factors to factors
steps.instruction: Loop over each column in `meta.df`; if the column is a factor, re‑factor it to ensure proper levels:

substeps.instruction: `for(x in colnames(meta.df)) { if(is.factor(meta.df[[x]])) { meta.df[[x]] %>% factor -> meta.df[[x]] } }`

steps.title: Reorder count columns to match metadata
steps.instruction: Select count‑table columns in the same order as the filtered metadata and store as `filt.count.tbl`:

substeps.instruction: `count.tbl %>% select(transcript, Chr, Strand, Start, End, Description, Gene, dir, tdir, match(meta.df$SampleID[meta.df$SampleID %in% colnames(.)], colnames(.))) -> filt.count.tbl`.
Verify ordering: `colnames(filt.count.tbl)[grepl("(BC|RB)", colnames(filt.count.tbl))] == meta.df$SampleID` should return all TRUE.

steps.title: Define DESeq2 model factors
steps.instruction: Identify factor columns for the statistical model, excluding `SampleID`, `Label`, `Replicate`, `Notes`, and any `excluded.factors`: `factorNames <- setdiff(colnames(meta.df), c("SampleID","Label","Replicate","Notes", excluded.factors))`.

steps.title: Create count matrix for DESeq2
steps.instruction: Extract barcode columns from `count.tbl`, convert to a matrix, and set row names to transcript IDs:

steps.title: Run DESeq2 analysis
steps.instruction: Create a DESeq2 dataset from the count matrix and metadata using a formula that includes all identified factors, then run the DESeq pipeline:

substeps.instruction: `dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(count.mat, meta.df, as.formula(paste0("~ ", paste(factorNames, collapse=" + ")))) %>% DESeq`.

steps.title: Create base table with raw and VST counts
steps.instruction: Copy the original count table, rename raw count columns with metadata labels, add the VST matrix (rounded to two decimals), and initialise a minimum p‑value column:

steps.title: Fetch DESeq2 results for each contrast
steps.instruction: Iterate over `resultList`, obtain results (using `lfcShrink` if `l2FCShrink` is TRUE), format columns, and merge into the base table:

substeps.instruction: `results.df <- if(l2FCShrink){ as.data.frame(lfcShrink(dds, contrast=rn, type = "ashr")) } else { as.data.frame(results(dds, contrast=rn)) }`

steps.title: Write final results CSV
steps.instruction: Calculate the minimum adjusted p‑value across all comparisons for each gene and write the table to a gzipped CSV named with the shrinkage option, result source, and analysis date:

substeps.instruction: `write.csv(dds.withCounts.tbl, row.names=FALSE, gzfile(sprintf("DE_%s_VST_%s_%s.csv.gz", if(l2FCShrink){"shrunk"} else {"orig"}, resultSource, analysisDate)))`

steps.instruction: Export the filtered and mitochondrial tables to an Excel file with separate sheets:

substeps.instruction: `write.xlsx2(as.data.frame(filtered.dds.tbl), sprintf("DE_%s_VST_%s_%s.xlsx", if(l2FCShrink){"shrunk"} else {"orig"}, resultSource, analysisDate), sheetName="Genome Data", row.names=FALSE)`
`write.xlsx2(as.data.frame(MT.dds.tbl), sprintf("DE_%s_VST_%s_%s.xlsx", if(l2FCShrink){"shrunk"} else {"orig"}, resultSource, analysisDate), sheetName="MT Data", append=TRUE, row.names=FALSE)`

steps.title: Add worksheets for each non‑Experiment contrast
steps.instruction: For each contrast in `resultList` that is not an "Experiment" factor, create a worksheet containing raw and adjusted counts plus DE results for genes with `padj ≤ 0.1`, sorted by descending log2FC:

substeps.instruction: `write.xlsx2(as.data.frame(res.tbl), sprintf("DE_%s_VST_%s_%s.xlsx", if(l2FCShrink){"shrunk"} else {"orig"}, resultSource, analysisDate), sheetName=sheetName, append=TRUE, row.names=FALSE);`
